seal.statement: A deterministic five-node cold-formation simulator on the in-process path - virtual clock, seeded in-memory transport, real owners throughout, and a guard that throws on any ambient clock or timer read in deterministic mode - reproduces the seed-starvation signature of main (seed gap fraction at least 50 percent with every joiner under 5 percent, incomplete-lease observations naming all five nodes with escalating backoff, prioritySpreadGap non-decreasing with zero operations in flight, admission ending in control_plane_pressure) at the calibration's own costs, two runs of one seed produce byte-identical reports, a run completes in under 60 seconds of real time, and a live report plus its log archive can be ingested as a canonical scenario. The scheduler charges every exclusive attribution segment, counted as dispatchCount plus handoffCount, at the owner's calibrated mean from the committed table, and holds an explicit causality invariant: each node has its own busyUntil, a segment advances it, work that becomes logically due while the node is busy cannot execute until the node is available, global execution takes the earliest causally runnable event, and no cross-node delivery precedes sender completion plus link delay.

text: Amendments 1 to 3 implemented against the sealed contract. (1) The calibration loader now classifies an owner the run never observed as calibrated:false with usPerSegment null instead of 0, gives it no cost-table entry, and the charger throws uncalibrated_owner when any segment reaches it; a measured owner whose file claims a zero mean is now calibration_invalid rather than a free owner. worker_dispatch is the one observed-inactive owner. (2) The charging unit was already dispatchCount + handoffCount in OwnerTurnMeter; it now has a witness that a synchronous runFormationOwner handoff costs the destination owner exactly one segment while the enclosing owner keeps exactly its own. (3) The causality invariant gained a five-clause falsifier. Clauses 1 to 4 already held in VirtualNetwork through maybeDeferForBusyNode and earliest-due selection. Clause 5 did not: send timed a message from the global clock, so a node busy to 2255 ms delivered at 5 ms. send now times from max(now, sender busyUntil) when a cost table is present, which is the sending side of the rule maybeDeferForBusyNode already applies on the receiving side. Without a cost table busyUntil never exceeds now, so every network without one is byte-identical; all four cost-table suites stay green (20, 17, 14, 15 passing). The probe metric is unchanged at 3.

Why the baseline does not reproduce the signature, measured rather than assumed. The three unmet probe conditions are not a cost-model failure and do not trigger the no-coefficient-tuning guard: they are owner surfaces the runner does not host yet, which its own header records. At seed 1 over a 22.2 s window the seed charges readiness 13197 ms of 13732 ms busy, and bootstrap, raft_apply, transport and admin charge zero milliseconds on every node because none of those owners runs. Against the calibration that is the wrong mix entirely: live bootstrap was 218903 segments, raft_apply 24680, transport 132244, admin 45510, and readiness only 330 segments at 0.4 percent of the window. The seed shows 15282 raft_protocol segments against 3431284 live, two orders of magnitude short, because replicas are scenario data rather than 135 initialised replicas across 45 system tables. readinessObservations is empty and admissionTransitions is empty, so the lease and admission conditions have nothing to judge rather than wrong values. The fixed-mean model is therefore untested by this run: the rate is wrong, not the mean. What the next slices owe is hosting bootstrap replica initialisation, the apply seam, transport, and the admission snapshot, so the owners produce their own rates as the contract requires.

Amendment 7 implemented: the calibration's unattributed share is carried as a band and never priced. The loader exposes window.unattributedPercent as calibration.residualPercent, the report records it under formationMetrics.calibrationResidual with priced false and the rule text, and decisionGrade(advantage, residual) classifies a claimed advantage no larger than the band as not decision-grade, including an unmeasured advantage. The witness also checks no owner absorbs the residual: charged owner time never exceeds the window. Nine tests pass; the probe metric is unchanged at 3, since the band is reporting rather than signature.

The quest worktree now carries the binding design text. Its solve/epics/formation-seed-decoupling/design.md was the pre-amendment note; it is replaced by the version committed on main as 1c9f62017, so the quest works against the ten amendments rather than the superseded ranking and sweep rules. The branch will still have to rebase onto main before it lands, and this file is where that conflict will be.

Round 1 rejects three of four items and is right on all three. (1) Observed-inactive owners: approved, with four latent zero-cost paths named. (2) Charging unit: rejected. The assertion that the enclosing owner keeps exactly its own segment passes by accident, because the outermost runFormationOwner sits at depth 0 and counts no handoff, so the 1 came from one promise continuation; a synchronous pass with no handoff charges zero segments, and meter.pass diffs global counters after its await, so segments a pass leaves behind are billed to whichever node passes next. (3) Causality: the send fix is correct and proven red on revert at the recorded 2255 and 5 ms, and the four cost-table suites plus four no-cost-table consumers are green, but only clauses 3 and 5 of the five are actually asserted; per-node busyUntil and earliest-causally-runnable ordering are unfalsified, and both timing assertions use unbounded >= where exact equality holds. (4) The recorded diagnosis is rejected: the seed-starvation condition is a cost problem, not an unhosted-surface problem. Hosting the missing owners adds charged work to joiners, and charged work is monotone in busyUntil while the window is fixed, so it moves the every-joiner-under-5-percent clause strictly further from passing. Readiness is 96 to 99 percent of every joiner's busy time, 7020 segments on the seed against 330 live, because one getNodeReadiness call registers about 79 continuation segments at the most expensive mean in the table. The sealed no-coefficient-tuning constraint therefore applies and the finding returns to the owner.

CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS, replacing the earlier evidence entry, which the verifier rejected and which I have now falsified myself. The seed-starvation condition fails for a cost reason, not an unhosted-surface reason, so the sealed no-coefficient-tuning constraint applies and this returns to the owner rather than to another slice. Three measurements. First, direction: the clause requires every joiner under 5 percent, and joiners sit at 10.1 percent gap. Charged work is monotone in busyUntil and stretches only lengthen, while the window is fixed by the scenario deadline, so hosting bootstrap, transport, admin and apply adds joiner work and moves the clause strictly further from passing. The unhosted-surface story predicts the wrong direction. Second, composition: readiness is 77 to 80 percent of every joiner's segments and 29 percent of the seed's. The harness drives getNodeReadiness every 250 ms where the live seed ran it about every 1900 ms, and each simulated call registers about 79.8 counted segments where live each call produced about 4.1. Same owner, same seam: a 7.6x driving rate and a 19.5x internal composition, which is 145x its live share at the most expensive mean in the table, 1879.98 us. The rate is therefore the harness's choice, not the owner's, which contradicts the design's own rule that owner-produced turn rate is authoritative. Third, a metric question for the owner: the probe measures the gap fraction over stretches of at least 1000 ms, and the seed reads 10.9 percent there, but the seed's busy fraction is 62.7 percent against the live signature's seed blocked 63 percent. Under the live metric the seed half of the clause already reproduces; it fails only under the probe's stretch definition. Which of the two the signature means is an owner decision, and it is the second reason this is not an unhosted-surface finding.

Round-1 rejections repaired. The calibrated gate moved onto the invariant: calibratedEntry is the single door, so the public charge() can no longer cost an uncalibrated owner zero, an owner outside the known set refuses as uncalibrated_owner rather than throwing a raw TypeError, and a non-positive or non-integer segment count refuses instead of accumulating. The every-exclusive-segment constraint is now actually met: the outermost dispatch of a pass sits at depth zero, so the seam counts neither a dispatch nor a handoff for it, and a synchronous pass with no handoff cost nothing at all; the pass now charges its own opening segment. The charging-unit witness no longer passes by accident, and asserts the measured accounting: a synchronous pass with no handoff charges its owner 1, one handoff charges the destination 1 and the enclosing owner 2 (its prefix and its resumption), and three handoffs charge the destination 3 and the enclosing owner still 2. That last figure is an open question recorded for the owner: the seam counts one resumption per pass rather than one per handoff, so simulator and live calibration undercount identically, which is what reproduction needs, but it may not be what the seam should do. The causality witness now asserts all four clauses, including per-node availability and the ordering clause, with exact timings rather than lower bounds; it is falsified twice, once with the send fix reverted (clause 5, delivery at 5 ms against 2255) and once with the receiving-side defer neutered (clause 3). Nine simulator tests pass, the four cost-table suites stay at 20, 17, 14 and 15, lint is clean, and the probe metric is unchanged at 3.

Owner decision 2026-09-14 on the metric ambiguity, settling the question the corrected diagnosis raised. The signature means watchdog-observed event-loop gap fraction, not aggregate busy fraction, and the sealed predicate is unchanged: seed gap fraction at least 50 percent, every joiner under 5 percent. The evidence: the originating live run showed 61713 ms of gaps of at least 1 s inside a concentrated 93000 ms formation interval, 66.4 percent, with no joiner gaps, and the calibration independently observed 78831 ms of watchdog gaps in its 152097 ms window, about 52 percent. The calibration phrase seed blocked 63127 ms is milliseconds, not 63 percent, which is where my busy-fraction comparison went wrong. So the simulated 10.9 percent seed gap fraction is RED, and the 62.7 percent busy fraction is diagnostic evidence only. The predicate must not be replaced, weakened, reinterpreted or supplemented to pass. Many sub-second charged slices can produce a high busy fraction with no watchdog gap at all, which is exactly why busy fraction cannot stand in for the signature.

Watchdog semantics repaired at the owner boundary, ahead of the readiness-drive slice. The gap was previously derived from charged busy stretches, which the owner forbids: charged work and heartbeat lateness are different quantities. The production watchdog's rule is now a pure function, observeHeartbeat, exported from src/diagnostics/event-loop-gap-watchdog.js and used by the live tick itself, so live and simulated observers share one owner rather than a copied constant; the watchdog's own suite stays at 19 passing. The simulator gains formation-sim-gap-observer.js: one 250 ms heartbeat per node armed on the virtual timer queue, deferred by that node's own occupancy exactly as any other event is, recording a gap when a beat runs at least 1000 ms late and resetting the expectation from the actual callback time. The seed's heartbeat starts at the window, each joiner's at its join, as their processes would. No inspector and no sampling profiler: only the rule is shared. Per-gap owner attribution now reads the charged stretches as evidence about a gap rather than as its measurement. The witness proves the rule (a 1200 ms late beat is one gap and the next expectation comes from the callback time) and the distinction the owner named: a node taking many sub-second slices is genuinely busy past 2000 ms and observes zero gaps, while one long slice on another node is one gap, not a backlog. Measured after the change: seed gap 2173 ms of the window, 9.8 percent, one gap; joiners 1994 ms, 9.0 percent, one gap each. The predicate is unchanged and still red, as expected before the readiness-drive repair.

The readiness-drive slice now has its red structural witness, added before the repair. It asserts that neither the runner nor the owner-pass module calls getNodeReadiness directly, that neither declares a readiness cadence constant, and that the scenario object carries no readiness or owner-pass cadence key. It currently FAILS on the first clause, naming the runner's direct call, which is exactly the defect the slice removes. Because it reads the simulator's own source rather than its output, a later slice cannot reintroduce a harness-local readiness loop without turning it red, which is what the owner asked for: mutating or removing the real upstream trigger must change or eliminate the readiness work, and inserting a harness loop must fail the witness. The production causality trace that names the real initiator is running; the repair waits on it, because choosing a replacement cadence myself is the tuning the owner forbade.

Production causality of a readiness pass, traced. There is NO production timer that drives readiness, and no readiness-owned cadence exists anywhere in src: readiness is demand-driven and invalidation-driven. The owner of a pass is ReadinessPlanningSnapshotOwner, fronted by an OwnerKeyReconcileQueue, and its reconcile function is the only place in src wrapped in runReadinessActivity, so the seam counts a readiness segment only when that queue drains. Every getNodeReadinessSync asked inside a rebalancer or publication turn is attributed to those owners instead, because nesting inherits the outer owner. So 330 live segments means 80 planning-owner builds, not 80 readiness questions. The periodicity the calibration shows is borrowed from an upstream timer that never mentions readiness: HeartbeatService ticks every 5000 ms, writes its own node row, coalesced to one rewrite per 10000 ms of metadata staleness, and that write flows through CDC into the system-table cache, whose change rotates the node-local planning identity and enqueues a build. Five nodes over a 152 s window gives about 76 such writes plus a few structural ones at the joins, which is the measured 80; and 250 handoffs over 80 dispatches is about 3.1 awaits per build, the shape of the planning build itself. The simulator is therefore not merely mis-paced but MIS-CAUSED: it runs readiness on every joined node every 250 ms, about 3040 passes against production's 80, a 38x over-count, and charges them all to the readiness owner where production charges most readiness questions to rebalancer and membership_publication. The repair is to host HeartbeatService and the cache-change path on virtual time and delete the cadence constant, so the harness never names readiness at all.

Readiness drive ownership repaired: the harness no longer names readiness at all. Three changes. First, the readiness planning queue's drain was escaping onto the real setImmediate, so every build in a deterministic run happened outside virtual time, on no node's clock and charged to nobody; readinessPlanningScheduleDrainFn now schedules on the node's own virtual timer. Second, HeartbeatService is hosted per node on virtual time, with its interval built from re-arming one-shot timers, lifecycle readiness answered per node rather than from the NodeService singleton, and the authoritative reporter readback disabled because it is real IO this seam cannot serve; it starts for the seed at the window and for each joiner at its join, as their processes would. Third, a new dispatch bracket charges whatever owners the production seam reports from inside a scheduled callback, without the harness naming one, so the heartbeat's own chain produces the segments: it writes the node row, the cache change rotates the node-local planning identity, and the planning queue drains a build. The harness readiness and publication passes are deleted and the cadence constant is gone, so the structural falsifier is green. Measured against the previous run, same seed: seed readiness segments fall from 7109 to 810 against 330 live, joiners from thousands to 7 to 18 each; seed busy falls from 62.7 to 10.4 percent and joiners from 10 to 48 percent down to 0.1 to 0.4 percent, which matches the live signature's no-joiner-gaps shape. Determinism holds, two runs hash identical, and eleven simulator tests pass. The probe stays at 3.

The drive repair changes the diagnosis, which is why it had to come before any judgement about missing surfaces. With the harness cadence gone, readiness is 810 seed segments against 330 live, the same order rather than 145 times its share, and the joiner clause is satisfiable at 0.0 percent where it was 10.1. What remains short is now genuinely volume the unbuilt slices owe: raft_protocol is 17121 seed segments against 3431284 live, about 200 times short, because replicas are scenario data rather than 135 initialised replicas across 45 system tables, and bootstrap, raft_apply, transport and admin still produce nothing at all against 218903, 24680, 132244 and 45510 live. The seed's gap fraction is 0.0 percent and its busy fraction 10.4 percent, so the starvation clause is far from met and no coefficient touches that: the seed is not doing the work. This is the point at which the earlier unhosted-surface story becomes true, and it was not true before, because readiness was drowning the measurement. One further seam repair fell out of hosting the real initiator, recorded separately: membership-publication-planning-evidence read the ambient clock unconditionally through an eagerly evaluated default argument, even on the calls that supplied a time source, and the deterministic guard threw on it.

Proof for the two production seam changes, run through the project's own change selection rather than a suite I picked: node scripts/select-change-tests.js over membership-publication-planning-evidence.js and event-loop-gap-watchdog.js widened to 629 files across seven batches plus the spine, and every one passed, 22086 assertions, no failures, including the membership-consistency, failure-scenarios, multi-node-cluster and preflight-critical-path-hops integration suites. The ambient-time repair is revert-red as the bounded-seams constraint requires: restoring the eager default argument makes the deterministic simulator throw nondeterministic_owner_seam, Date.now read inside rebalancer dispatch, naming resolveNowMs itself, and restoring the lazy fallback makes the run complete again. The watchdog extraction is behaviour-preserving by construction, because the live tick now calls the same pure rule it previously inlined, and the watchdog's own 19 tests pass. This is self-proof; the slice still owes independent verification before it lands.

Round 2 rejects four of six items and is right on every one. The central rejection: 99.6 percent of the seed's remaining 810 readiness segments still come from the harness, not the heartbeat. Ablation on a scratch copy gives 810 with both, 812 with the heartbeat off, and 12 with the planning-gate round off, so the marginal attribution is 803 to the gate pass and 3 to the heartbeat; sweeping the gate cadence moves readiness linearly, 1613 at 125 ms through 110 at 2000 ms. The planning gate reads readiness synchronously and enqueues builds six times per round, so I renamed the cadence rather than removing it. Worse, the structural falsifier is a source grep and was defeated in the verifier's scratch copy by a renamed constant and a computed property name, leaving all eleven tests green while a full harness readiness cadence was restored at 8858 seed segments. Second rejection: the chain I claimed does not execute at all. SystemTableCache.notifyListeners dispatches every cache-change listener through a bare real setImmediate, and the whole run completes inside one macrotask because flushMicrotasks only drains microtasks, so 46 notifications were scheduled and zero fired; handleCacheChange and recordTableChange were never called once. The heartbeat's row write is real and correctly coalesced at the production 5000 ms interval, but it invalidates nothing. Third: I passed no membershipPublicationService to the heartbeat, which production does, so its scheduled reconcile disabled itself and membership_publication fell from 309 seed segments to zero on every node against 15.5 percent of the live window. Fourth: my recorded baselines are wrong, 7020 and 61.79 percent rather than 7109 and 62.7, and I mixed metrics quoting a joiner move of 10.1 to 0.0 when the like-for-like observer figures are 9.0 and 9.8. Under the owner's metric the seed moved 9.8 percent to 0.0, strictly FURTHER from the clause. The gap observer is approved, with a real bias found: a joiner's observer starts at its join while windowMs is the whole window, so the last joiner watches 50 ms of a 20050 ms denominator and its fraction is structurally zero, flattering the very clause that now passes.

Two defects I introduced are repaired; the four rejections are not. resolveNowMs was NOT behaviour-preserving as I claimed: the helper it replaced coerced with Number, accepted zero and above, and truncated, so null became 0, the string 1234 became 1234 and 1234.7 became 1234, while my Number.isInteger and above-zero test sent every one of those to the ambient clock. Given this area's known Number(null) shape that is a real production regression, now restored to the original coercion exactly. The heartbeat's clearTimeoutFn was a no-op, so every attempt's 6 s watchdog stayed armed and recorded a timeout failure on attempts that had already succeeded, leaking one charged timer per attempt; it is now a cancellable handle. Neither changes the measurement: seed readiness stays 810 and busy 10.48 percent. The four rejections stand open and are the next work: the planning-gate cadence is still a harness cadence and owns 99.6 percent of readiness, the cache-change notify hop escapes to a real setImmediate that never fires so the heartbeat invalidates nothing, the heartbeat is not wired to the publication service it drives in production, and the structural falsifier is a source grep that a rename defeats.

Owner decision 2026-09-14 accepting all four rejections and redirecting the slice. No claim of movement toward or away from the signature may be made from the current run: the model is not yet causally comparable to production. The slice is now composition and event-causality fidelity, not reproduction. Seven requirements. One, remove harness ownership of readiness entirely rather than re-timing it; the planning gate may observe already-produced state but observation must be causally inert, proved by running the same scenario at substantially different observation frequencies and requiring identical owner segment counts and state transitions, and the scenario should not possess a callable readiness-evaluation capability at all. Two, restore the real cache-change asynchronous hop by authorizing a minimal src/cache seam: SystemTableCache accepts an injected next-turn dispatcher, production stays exactly setImmediate, the simulation places the callback on the node's deterministic queue at the current virtual time after the producing turn, executing once and preserving listener order; scheduling only, with no change to mutation, invalidation, batching or business logic, and no invented cache attribution owner. Three, scenario completion must mean no causally runnable deterministic event remains at or before the boundary, not that a promise chain returned, and not by flushing the host loop. Four, restore production composition for publication by reusing the production construction owner or extracting the smallest production-owned assembly both consume, never another harness wiring description, with an ablation proving removal suppresses the publication path. Five, the joiner denominator is a defect: each node's gap fraction is measured from its own observer start, the scenario end follows the formation contract's failure window after the final join, every node reports observer start, end, observed duration, qualifying gap time and fraction, and the predicate is REFUSED for a node without the minimum observation horizon. Six, replace the defeated source grep with behavioural and capability proofs. Seven, only then take a new baseline, and only after a causal census of zero harness readiness calls, notifications scheduled and fired equal and non-zero, real cache-change handler engagements non-zero, heartbeat mutations at the production cadence, publication activity non-zero, zero stranded events, and a valid observation horizon on every joiner. The frozen attribution accounting stays frozen: this slice makes the same production interactions happen, it does not change how they are counted.

Cache-change hop, publication composition and quiescence. One, SystemTableCache now accepts an injected next-turn dispatcher for cache-change notification, defaulting to exactly setImmediate(callback); the simulator supplies the node's deterministic queue, so the hop is an ordinary scheduled event rather than an escape the virtual clock never reaches. Delivery, listener order, batching, mutation and invalidation are untouched; no cache owner is invented, and the callback runs through the same owner-agnostic bracket, so whatever the production code inside declares is what gets counted. Two, production composition for publication: the heartbeat's construction, initialize and syncOwnerDependencies are extracted into assembleHeartbeatService in the production module, and BOTH control-plane-setup and the simulator now call it, so the collaborator list cannot drift again. That alone was not enough: the scheduled reconcile also gates on PARTITIONS.leader_node_id naming the local node, and the scenario's seeded partition rows carried no such field, so no node was ever the publication owner. The real cohort's elected leader is now written into every node's cache as CDC would carry it, and membership_publication is no longer structurally absent. Three, quiescence: the drive loop settles each step by draining the queue and flushing continuations until nothing further is runnable, and the scenario boundary retires every continuation the run started before the meter closes. That was a real determinism defect, not a tidiness point: the heartbeat dispatches its reconcile tick without awaiting it, and chains from one run were landing inside the next, so the same seed produced 6 publication segments in the first in-process run and 9 in every later one. Three consecutive in-process runs now give 6, 6, 6 with zero events runnable at the boundary, and the report carries strandedEvents. Eleven tests pass and the probe is unchanged at 3.

Per-node attribution leakage is now the dominant correctness problem, and it blocks the causal census the owner asked for. Real planning now runs from Raft leadership rather than a harness call, and the result exposes what round 2 already named as its first additional defect: OwnerTurnMeter diffs the process-global attribution counters and bills the delta to whichever node's bracket is open, so work leaks across nodes. The evidence is unambiguous. Every priority-partition rebalancer in the scenario is constructed on the SEED's hosts, and no rebalancer exists on any joiner, yet the report now charges joiners 336, 1357, 337 and 1641 rebalancer segments. Those segments cannot belong to those nodes. Cross-process determinism still holds, two runs hash identical, but in-process determinism does not: three consecutive simulate calls on one seed give 49, 8 and 50 publication segments on the seed, because owner work now interleaves across nodes inside one shared attribution window instead of being bracketed one pass at a time. Two consequences. First, no per-node figure in the current report can be trusted, so the census clauses that count per-node activity, and the joiner clause that reads a per-node gap fraction, cannot be evaluated yet. Second, the fix is per-node attribution context rather than a change to how segments are counted, which is the frozen part: the counting convention stays exactly as the one authorized calibration measured it. The likely shape is an async context keyed by node around each scheduled dispatch, so a continuation is billed to the node whose event it is.

Harness ownership of readiness and planning removed, and two further composition omissions repaired. The planner's own timers were armed with the ambient setTimeout, so the one owner that decides when a planning pass happens could not be hosted; setTimeoutFn and clearTimeoutFn are now injectable on the rebalancer and default to the ambient pair, leaving production unchanged. The simulator gives every owner timer the node's virtual queue through one cancellable one-shot, and planning now starts the way production starts it, from setLeader on Raft leadership acquisition, which enqueues a check and arms the periodic timer. The harness planning-gate round is deleted; what remains is an observeState call that only reads rows the owners have already written, and the sampling interval is now a parameter of simulate so a witness can vary it. Two omissions surfaced while doing this and are fixed: the seeded partition rows carried no leader_node_id, so publication ownership could never be true, and the RebalanceCoordinator was never initialized, so every operation creation threw RebalanceCoordinator is shutting down, a message the guard also raises for an uninitialized coordinator. With both fixed the run is free of error output. Cross-process determinism holds and the probe stays at 3, but in-process determinism is now broken by the attribution leakage recorded separately, so the cadence-invariance witness, the ablation witnesses and the causal census all wait on that repair.

Attribution context repair implemented as a context-only change; it now refuses the simulation, which is the designed behaviour and not a failure of the design. What is in place: execution node is a second, independent dimension carried in async-local storage, and the deterministic scheduler is its only authority, binding a frame around every callback it executes, destination node for a delivery and owning node for a timer. Nothing infers a node from an owner object, a row, a bracket or an owner name. Async resources capture both dimensions at creation in separate maps, deliberately so: releasing an owner's descendants rewrites only the owner map, so ownership can be released without the CPU moving to another node, and the owner map keeps exactly the string values every existing reader and every counterexample mutation expects. A dispatched resource's captured node overrides the ambient store for its own callback, which is what keeps a seed continuation on the seed after the scheduler has run joiner work. Snapshots gained an additive byExecutionNode breakdown that is empty unless a scheduler binds nodes, so the aggregate owner rows, counts and durations are untouched and live formation sees no change; the attribution suite is 97 passing, the cost-model suite 20, and a Raft election network suite 14. Node identity is not part of FORMATION_OWNER and there is still exactly one attribution window. The meter now charges from the per-node rows the seam recorded rather than from whichever bracket was open. What remains: the fail-closed rule refuses the run with formation_execution_node_unbound, and it is right to. I traced the offender to a readiness-owned promise created at segment depth 1 with no bound node, reached through the charged dispatch path, and wrapping the meter's whole async body in the frame did not clear it. That is one more unbound seam to find, which is exactly what the rule exists to surface, and I am not going to widen the rule to get a green run.

Owner decision 2026-09-14 on the refusal. The narrowing stands: formation_execution_node_unbound applies only to a segment with a real formation owner and no execution node, and unattributed harness plumbing may be node-less. No fallback may be added, not the current runner node, not the trigger resource's node, not owner.nodeId, not the seed, not the most recently executed scheduler node; the refusal stays hard until the missing boundary is understood, and the current refusal counts as success. The next step is provenance rather than repair: capture, for the first unbound attributed resource, its type, asyncId and triggerAsyncId, the captured owner, the current active owner, the attribution depth, both async-local values, whether the trigger has a captured owner and node and what they are, the current scheduler event id, kind and execution node, and a debug-only creation stack, plus the stack of the runFormationOwner entry that made readiness active. Counting and scheduling must not change to obtain it. The trace then classifies the bug into one of four buckets: readiness entered outside any scheduler frame, which means the missing seam is upstream and must be routed through the production scheduling boundary rather than bound inside runReadinessActivity; readiness entered inside a correct frame but a child resource losing the node, which means the propagation itself is defective; a scheduler-bound drain whose later continuation escapes, which means one precise promise or timer boundary needs seaming; or plumbing outside node execution that inherited readiness ownership accidentally, which would be an ownership-propagation bug rather than a node-propagation one. The suspect to inspect first is the readiness planning owner's reconcile queue boundary, but the transition must be proved, not assumed. One directed pair of attribution tests is required: a promise created inside a bound seed readiness frame must resume as seed plus readiness after unrelated joiner work runs, and unattributed plumbing created outside every frame may stay node-less but must throw if it later enters readiness without first entering a scheduler node frame.

Provenance captured, bug classified as bucket B, repaired; a second escape remains and I am stopping on it as instructed. The trace named the offender exactly: a PROMISE, asyncId 240 from trigger 238, captured owner readiness, active owner readiness, depth 1, owner store null, execution frame NULL, trigger owner unattributed with a null node, created inside AsyncLocalStorage.run through runOnExecutionNode, with the owner entered at runReadinessActivity from the readiness planning owner's reconcileFn under OwnerKeyReconcileQueue.drain. Execution frame null while the creation stack sat inside a live frame is bucket B, a defect in my own propagation rather than a missing upstream seam, and the readiness queue was not guilty. Two bugs in one line: the dispatched-node stack stored bare node ids where the reader expected frames, and a dispatch whose resource captured no node pushed a null that SHADOWED the scheduler's live frame, so work executing inside a correctly bound frame reported no node. A dispatch with no captured node now defers to the ambient frame instead of hiding it. That cleared readiness and exposed the next unbound seam honestly: raft_protocol entered at LifeRaft's constructor, which calls heartbeat during construction, from the cohort's construct outside any frame; construction happens in the node's own process in production, so the scheduler binds the node around it. The simulation now runs with no refusal. The invariant the owner named holds: only the seed constructs rebalancers, and joiner rebalancer segments are exactly 0, 0, 0, 0 where the leaked run showed 336, 1357, 337 and 1641. Cross-process determinism is restored and the attribution suite is back to 97 passing after I restored the parameter name a counterexample mutation depends on. Same-process repeatability is NOT green: three runs of one seed give hashes matching for the first two and differing on the third, with seed raft_protocol 8936, 8936, 8934 and rebalancer 4024, 4024, 3969. Per the standing instruction that is a second deterministic escape rather than an attribution issue, so the census, the falsifiers and the ablations stay blocked and I stop here.
